panel title atlassian update nov borderstyle solid bordercolor ebf f titlebgcolor ebf f bgcolor ffffff epics behave slightly differently in next gen projects and this is one example of that we are formalizing an issue hierarchy in next gen projects where we will have parent child relationships rather than using epic links this will facilitate some cool stuff int he future around reporting and roll up estimation unfortunately in the short term it means when you move issues to next gen projects you will need to manually assign these issues to the relevant epic it s important to note the epic link has not actually been removed in the background it s just not visible and is not useful within the context of the next gen project if you were to move your issues back to a classic project for example you would not lose this linkage although the epic name and epic colour custom fields would be lost in the future as we build out the next gen projects we will provide an automated mechanism to create the new parent child relationship based on the epic link but it just isn t something we have got to yet we apologize we didn t make this clear earlier we have updated our docs in an attempt to clarify how epics behave when migrating projects you can review the docs from this page cheers atlassian panel h summary when an epic from a non next gen project is moved to a next gen project the association is removed all issues associated with the epics will no longer be linked to the epic h steps to reproduce have projects next gen and non next gen create an epic from a non next gen project add a child issue to the epic move the epic to the next gen project h expected result epic link remains the issues are still linked with the epic in the next gen project even after the move or have a better communication around this so user would be aware of this prior to the move h actual result epic link is lost

when we access the pr api in bitbucket or github we only receive a string which is the username of the user and for bitbucket a uuid we don t get the email when we are trying to attach a user to a pr we only have this username string to work with so we then perform a lookup to see what emails are available for that username we then filter through those emails either returning a single match or if there are multiple emails one that matches the username when there are multiple combinations of author and commiter values across changesets however this can confuse the user association in some rare cases we are getting the wrong user associated in this situation you have changesets where the same author name is associated with different emails or there are overlaps between different users for author and commiter this goes through username email filtering resulting in incorrect user association a typical scenario that could cause this would be two commits structured like this hash author name author email abc susan email xyz susan email or alternatively hash author name author email commiter name commiter email abc susan email someone else email to check for this data you can run which will output the author and commiter from the git repository if these are not the same or if the single author name maps to multiple emails then this may lead to incorrect user association

we are presently collecting feedback on our spike of multiple project support within greenhopper current information can be found on ghs this is a spike that was developed with no formal structure or testing we are trying to get an idea of what greenhopper will look like with multiple projects there will be bugs we will throw all of this code away and we may not ever support multiple projects there are no guarantees you can create an account on the customer sandbox and play around with the functionality some points to note are outlines below current functionality restrictions individual projects can no longer be selected the page title and project icon will not reflect the selected project shared versions will only appear if the all projects selected match the all projects the shared version exists in exactly within a selection of projects only the issue type scheme and permission scheme can be different existing versions with the same name will not be linked in greenhopper only shared versions created through greenhopper will be linked selecting the scrum project template will no longer change the issue type scheme in the selected projects but will still change the other settings on the fly can no longer be selected as a context tips to choose which projects to select create a new context or manage edit an existing one creating a version in greenhopper will create a shared version across all of the selected projects ranking is now global so changes in rank will affect all contexts that means that every issue in jira has a relative rank to every other issue all schemes except for issue type and permission schemes should be the same across all projects that are selected deleting or releasing versions that are part of a shared version through jira ie not through the greenhopper interface will is strongly discouraged it will likely not work configurations selected through tools configuration will now configure based on the selected context instead of project
